parsed.rationale: All 16 participating records are `type-alias-object` declarations with empty `fields_or_signature` lists and a `shared_field_count` of 1, meaning the only shared structural signal is the empty-body shape of a SwiftUI `PreviewProvider` or local type alias — not any shared semantic content. The names are entirely distinct domain concepts (`ConfettiView`, `DebugHUD`, `WallpaperListView`, `HeightReader`, `PlaycutLoadingSection`, `InfoDetailView`, etc.) spread across unrelated packages (`PartyHorn`, `DebugPanel`, `Wallpaper`, `WXUI`, `MusicShareKit`, `PlayerHeaderView`, `app:WatchXYC`, `app:iOS`). The structural coincidence is that SwiftUI preview scaffolding and local view-alias declarations all produce zero-field type-alias objects; there is no shared logic, no shared interface, and no meaningful abstraction to extract. Consolidating these would couple unrelated UI packages for no benefit.
